output.explanation: After finalising, the test waits a fixed 2 seconds and then checks the address once with `expect(page.url()).toContain('/Invoices/Details/')`. Posting to the ledger takes a variable time, so on slower runs the posting page is still showing when the check runs. The suite already has `invoice.waitUntilPosted()` for this, and the test uses it after the credit note but not after the invoice.
evidence: All 6 failures out of 20 runs have the same message, `Error: expect(received).toContain(expected) // indexOf`. The only `toContain` in the test is `expect(page.url()).toContain('/Invoices/Details/')`, which runs straight after `await page.waitForTimeout(2000);`.

Help page 22 says the posting page shows while the invoice is posted to the general ledger, and that this 'can take a few seconds, depending on how busy the ledger is'. A fixed 2-second wait therefore cannot always be enough.
InvoicePage.waitUntilPosted() waits for the URL to match /Invoices/Details/, which is the page-based wait the conventions require ('Tests wait for the page, never for a fixed time').

No test running alongside explains the failures. BR-08 ran in all 6 failed and all 14 passed runs. BR-10 ran in 4 of 6 failed runs and all 14 passed runs. BR-01, BR-12 and BR-16 ran in no failed runs.

The only shared-data entry is BR-11 on customer C180, through project P-1080, with no recorded changes. This test uses its own project, P-1081 Pacific customs integration, so shared data does not explain the failures. The material does not show whether a busy ledger caused the slow runs.
output.fix_summary: Replace the fixed 2-second wait and the one-off URL check with `invoice.waitUntilPosted()`, and wait for the invoice number with a web-first assertion before reading it.
